CLAUDE.md: The contributor guide preserves SmartCard-only backend borrowing, KDF aliases, historical credential identity, X25519/ATT defects, version provenance and precise assertion limits. Its initialization fallback is narrower than actual backend handling: every non-OK or short successful version response falls back. Preserve the existing qualifications while correcting only that local explanation.
README.md: All complete task bodies were read with imports and enclosing resources: device convenience factories own hidden connections; direct creation borrows; PIN inputs/DER/private keys remain caller-owned; KDF provisioning retains outer objects and clears caller arrays; verifier/certificate/result lifetimes are explicit. Sequential-operation advice is useful. Add precise exchange-versus-workflow and effective-version/SCP-reset conditions only where needed. Existing historical defect, ATT exception, ROCA, trust and sample caveats remain substantive rather than evidence of repaired behavior.
PACKAGE_README.md: The short package page describes applet tasks, alpha/security-audit status, transitive Core and links. Its install fragment carries no connection, key, prompt or secret result lifetime and needs no boundary-specific expansion; detailed task constraints are linked.
AccessChangeAdminPinCommand.cs: The command obtains two disposable credential owners and awaits ChangeAdmin before they leave scope; known-current verification is performed by that applet method rather than a separate Verify. Supplied option strings outlive byte-owner disposal and the helper uses no confirmation reader. Keep runtime/help unchanged and retain PGP-IMP-015 input policy scope.
AccessChangePinCommand.cs: The command owns current/new byte owners through awaited ChangePin and handles null input. It applies the generic credential helper rather than card C4 byte validation, and no new-PIN confirmation call occurs. Source strings and device persistent change have separate lifetimes; a success message establishes no independent state readback.
AccessSetResetCodeCommand.cs: Admin verification and Reset Code write are sequential awaited operations under one borrowed session callback. Two disposable inputs remain alive through transmission. Reader length and card limits remain distinct; clearing option-derived bytes leaves immutable command-line strings.
AccessSetRetriesCommand.cs: Admin verification precedes three-count mutation; the session validates 1..255 and leaves family/device acceptance to the card. The command displays requested values rather than independent readback. Preserve NEO default-credential effects and capability gaps under PGP-IMP-010/015.
AccessUnblockPinCommand.cs: The command separately collects Reset Code/new User PIN, retains both disposable owners through the reset-code route and reports completion. It neither borrows an Admin credential nor conditionally ignores a credential. It adds no card-profile byte checks or post-reset authentication assertion.
CertificatesDeleteCommand.cs: Slot parsing/confirmation precedes credential collection, Admin verification and awaited deletion. The supplied session remains owned by the command base. ATT public certificate deletion is independent of private-key erasure and reset; existing destructive task caveats remain applicable.
CertificatesExportCommand.cs: The returned X509 object is not disposed; PEM/DER export branches use it and public output bytes need no secret erasure. DER branch disposes its stdout stream, not the certificate. Existing remarks accurately identify the missing owner and leave trust validation separate.
CertificatesImportCommand.cs: File loading occurs before Admin input; the loaded certificate survives every return/exception without a disposal scope. Its subject/issuer/thumbprint display is metadata, never a trusted key-binding check. Existing comments retain that PGP-IMP-015 lifetime gap rather than advertising complete cleanup.
InfoCommand.cs: The command refreshes app data, separately reads retries/counter/UIF and displays each known slot. Key status is inferred from nonempty fingerprint length, including zero-filled fields; current comment directs decisions to ListKeyInformation. Once display says per session although card access state is the real boundary; this executable string is retained under the existing tool finding, not edited here.
KeysAttestCommand.cs: The settings declare --pin, while execution directly invokes Attest on a fresh session without reading/verifying that input; returned certificate is undisposed. Metadata/PEM display establishes neither signature/key binding nor chain trust. Existing caveat accurately preserves the engineering finding.
KeysGenerateCommand.cs: Admin input remains scoped through awaited Spectre status callback and generation; algorithm strings choose concrete ordinary algorithms, with no ROCA guard or capability proof beyond session checks. The command parser accepts ATT despite narrower help; malformed ATT CRT and persistent partial attribute changes remain qualified.
KeysImportCommand.cs: PEM is read into an immutable string; PKCS8 DER is cleared in finally and returned private-key owner is disposed after import. RSA/EC PEM branches export private parameters into temporary arrays before SDK cloning; disposing providers/SDK keys leaves those separate exports outside explicit cleanup. Link C's private-array/provider ownership and existing PGP-IMP-015 rather than claiming the DER finally clears every producer.
KeysSetTouchCommand.cs: The command reads current UIF, refuses fixed values, confirms selected fixed policy, verifies Admin and writes policy. Its actual UI still overstates factory-reset recovery for ATT, accurately qualified by the current comment/README. Preserve output and the irreversible ATT replacement boundary.
OpenPgpCommand.cs: The base selects one eligible SmartCard device, opens an owned convenience session, awaits the complete command and asynchronously disposes before handling failure. No user-presence service/token is supplied. Provided strings encode directly into an owned pool buffer without reader limits; interactive/redirected Core reader behavior differs. The helper wording about application enforcement needs a responsibility-versus-mechanism distinction.
ResetCommand.cs: The status callback awaits Reset, then prints default credentials without full readback. Existing remarks qualify unchecked statuses and ATT persistence, while executable ALL/private-key/factory-reset wording stays unchanged under the old sample finding. No independent state restoration is implemented by this command.
OutputHelpers.cs: Delegated formatting/confirmation helpers forward public strings and data; WriteError writes raw exception text to stderr. This is diagnostic provenance rather than a central secret-redaction boundary. No helper creates a session, owns a credential or verifies a device result.
DeviceSelector.cs: The actual selector delegates to Cli.Shared with SmartCard-only eligibility and FirstEligible noninteractive policy; noninteractive diagnostics are redirected to stderr. It passes a cancellation token but the command base invokes it with default. Selection is not independent physical identity attestation or authorisation for mutation.
OpenPgpTool.csproj: The sample references OpenPgp/Core/Management/Cli.Shared/Cli.Commands and Spectre/Hosting packages; it is nonpackable and suppresses only the named example analyzer. Project configuration is retained, compilation and analyzer participation remain later gates; references supply no execution evidence.
Program.cs: The complete command tree registers info/reset/access/keys/certificates and invokes the Spectre runner synchronously. Reset's executable all-data description remains within PGP-IMP-015. Registration creates no SCP/prompt/credential policy or extra connection lifetime.
AlgorithmAttributes.cs: RSA parse/encoding retains modulus/exponent/import format with explicit big-endian fields. EC factories consult Core concrete identity and module representation, choose construction/slot ID and reject non-EC; parsing retains received algorithm and trailing FF format while unknown OIDs fail. Default direct initialization and malformed/unknown admission remain PGP-IMP-018; exact roundtrip tests do not establish device support.
ApplicationRelatedData.cs: The parser owns/disposes the outer Tlv and obtains independently copied dictionary values. It decodes optional extended lengths/GFM and mandatory AID/discretionary algorithms, with old outer-level fallback. HistoricalBytes remains a dictionary-owned copy rather than an alias of the disposed outer TLV. Unknown mandatory algorithms can prevent typed session creation before raw GetData is available; an independent RawSmartCardSession is the lower-tier diagnostic route.
IOpenPgpBackend.cs: The internal backend contract contains only initialization and APDU Send. It introduces no IDisposable or key/prompt ownership, consistent with ApplicationSession retaining the effective protocol owner.
OpenPgpBackend.cs: Initialization selects OpenPGP, activates/reselects on 6285/6985, then reads version. Send forwards throwOnError/token unchanged. GetVersion uses throwOnError false: every non-OK/short successful response falls through to 1.0.0, unlike its narrower old-firmware comment. With an SCP wrapper, Select is plain and subsequent Send remains secure; no reset handshake is added.
BcdHelper.cs: DecodeByte computes two nibbles without rejecting A..F; TryDecodeSerial rejects either invalid nibble and resets output. OpenPGP version and AID callers use different contracts. Valid six-case BCD tests do not establish malformed-version rejection; keep identity raw bytes and backend fallback policy separate.
OpenPgpCredentialOptions.cs: Three factories set text-reader limits User 6..127, Admin/Reset 8..127 with UTF8 default inherited from Core. They implement no card C4/profile validation; source already distinguishes encoding byte length. Add exact UTF16 units and actual CLI bypass conditions without importing CTAP policy.
Crt.cs: Ordinary static CRTs encode empty B6/B8/A4 values. ATT builds an inner 84 TLV then passes only inner.Value to B6, yielding B60181; the correct vendor nested encoding is B603840181. Borrowed static output must stay read-only. Preserve the confirmed ATT read defect and separate target-key FB attestation.
DataObject.cs: The enum carries full/nested tags with object-specific access caveats, UTF8 language-pair semantics and metadata identifiers. No blanket direct-access prohibition follows from container grouping. This is public nonsecret numeric metadata, not an owned secret TLV or universal card capability declaration.
DigestInfo.cs: The helper borrows a fixed public header and returns header+digest bytes; hashes supported are SHA1/256/384/512. The caller session constructs DigestInfo and the card supplies RSA padding. Literal-header tests compare full headers, while Build checks shape/selected digest endpoints; no standalone host/provider execution occurred.
DiscretionaryDataObjects.cs: Dictionary field copies feed mandatory capabilities/algorithms/PW status and optional collections/UIFs. Fingerprints receive independent per-entry arrays; timestamp four-byte bit assembly uses signed int and zero remains unspecified. Unknown slot IDs are skipped, known unknown status values survive and incomplete collection tails are ignored. Preserve PGP-IMP-018 and avoid secret cleanup requirements for public metadata by default.
EcImportFormat.cs: Standard/StandardWithPubkey are protocol encoding values 0/FF, not device support claims. PrivateKeyImport currently emits private-only templates; directly modeled optional public material has its own caller lifetime.
ExtendedCapabilities.cs: The parser requires at least ten bytes, reads challenge/certificate/special-DO lengths as big-endian uint16 and retains flag/SM bytes. Boolean fields test equality to 1; extensions are ignored. These advertised sizes are not automatically enforced by all session operations, retained under PGP-IMP-010.
ExtendedCapabilityFlags.cs: The byte bit assignments distinguish KDF, AES, changeable algorithms, private use, PW status, import, challenge and secure messaging. Presence of an enum flag alone grants no Core SCP profile or applet enforcement guarantee.
ExtendedLengthInfo.cs: Disposable decoded TLVs yield first request and later response values for repeated tag02; sizes are metadata and are not passed into Pcsc.Configure by OpenPGP. Extra tag02 entries overwrite response max; short values fail. No advertised-bound enforcement is inferred from this model.
GeneralFeatureManagement.cs: The public flags describe card-reported hardware features; UIF encoding uses Button. This enum does not establish a prompt-service lifetime, live touch event or host device capability.
GenerationTimes.cs: The read-only dictionary stores signed int carriers with explicit unsigned four-octet seconds and zero-sentinel interpretation. The current XML already handles high-bit timestamps; retain the historical PGP-C022 extension of PGP-IMP-018 rather than treating documentation as a fixed representation.
IOpenPgpSession.cs: The complete interface was read despite only three assigned parser units. It accurately records borrowed UTF8 inputs, persistent partial writes, KDF aliases, credential identity defect, output formats, ATT exceptions and reset limits. PutKey's current supported-curve list lags actual secp256k1/Brainpool representation. The interface preamble needs entry-versus-admitted cancellation precision; typed raw inspection requires successful typed initialization or a separate raw session.
IYubiKeyExtensions.cs: SmartCard-only resolution and immutable options copy precede generic connection helper. Success transfers the hidden connection only after direct initialization; the internal existing-connection overload stays borrowed. Source factory selection is explicit and has no fallback to HID or a second transport on failure.
Ins.cs: The internal enum retains instruction bytes for PIN, crypto, activation, key management, SELECT DATA, raw access, version/retries and attestation. Wire construction stays visible in session methods; no command-object or execution state is hidden here.
Kdf.cs: KdfNone returns a caller-owned PIN copy. S2K setters clone salts/hashes, Process clears concatenated salt+PIN in finally and IncrementalHash is scoped. Count is unsigned32 expanded bytes and at least one full input, distinct from packet coding. ToBytes disposes TLVs but copies EncodeList's owned return again; Parse clones DecodeDictionary's initial hashes without clearing source copies. Dispose clears current backing arrays without a disposed guard, so aliased session use after caller disposal changes derivation.
KeyFingerprints.cs: The sealed read-only dictionary receives an exclusively owned parser dictionary and exposes ReadOnlyMemory values. Repeated parse test proves separate backing arrays; read-only views are not universal immutability against unsafe/writable owner access. Public fingerprint metadata has no secret cleanup obligation.
KeyInformation.cs: The sealed collection stores a parser-owned dictionary, exposes only read-only dictionary operations and retains known-slot status bytes. It is the relevant key-presence source rather than fingerprint length. Reflection tests check surface shape, not hardware truth.
KeyRef.cs: The four slot values map through one switch to attributes/UIF/time/fingerprint/CRT. Ordinary mappings and static memory are public protocol metadata. ATT mapping preserves its malformed CRT qualification and persistent vendor exception; invalid slot values throw.
KeyStatus.cs: None/Generated/Imported describe reported origin status, not independent manufacturer or host trust. OpenPgpTool's fingerprint-length display should not be mistaken for this typed status.
OpenPgpAid.cs: The parser checks minimum14, clones raw AID, BCD-decodes version and tries BCD serial before negating a signed cast of raw uint32. Current XML correctly warns that high-bit invalid-BCD values may be positive. AID card version, applet GET VERSION and physical metadata remain different provenance.
OpenPgpInvalidPinException.cs: The exception retains SW and nullable retry count for VerifyPin/VerifyAdmin only. XML already qualifies broad non-PIN failure mapping, extended Reset-counter mismatch and supported User recovery. No new Core status-decoder fix closes applet identity/error policy.
OpenPgpKeyInfo.cs: Frozen module metadata derives ordinary named-curve OIDs from Core and adds legacy Ed/X25519 overrides plus RSA2048/3072/4096. DER value-octet encoding is cached nonsecret metadata; no secret AsnWriter cleanup finding applies. Optional metadata and exact OID lookup are representation, not a provider/card support assertion.
OpenPgpSession.Certificates.cs: Ordinary SELECT DATA then GET/PUT/empty write spans separate guarded exchanges; ATT uses FC directly. Certificate parsing returns a new caller-owned X509 object, with ordinary6A88 absence only after successful selection. Workaround prefix depends on effective feature version. Public certificate TLV payloads are not private keys; occurrence selection is shared device state without whole-workflow exclusion.
OpenPgpSession.Config.cs: UIF writes update override cache after success; algorithm writes leave cached crypto attributes stale. Algorithm list unpacks/pads the outer TLV, skips unknown inner tags/rejected attrs, preserves order/multiplicity and applies pre5.6.1 workaround only outside major zero. GetKdf returns alias; SetKdf serializes without cleanup and installs exact input, dropping prior reference. Existing Python-canonical wording is comparator provenance, not normative authority.
OpenPgpSession.Crypto.cs: Full payload/notification/formatting methods were read: RSA/ECDSA hash, EdDSA copies raw input; Decipher wraps ordinary EC but passes X25519 raw. Results have branch-specific transfer/clear scopes and callback-resolution ordering. Empty/malformed ECDSA response can fail formatting, with raw cleanup retained. Core transport/chaining/SCP staging remains a separate producer graph.
OpenPgpSession.Keys.cs: Generate sets attributes before generation; PutKey owns import copies, clears serialized template and refreshes only after success; Delete uses two destructive attribute writes. All span multiple exchanges. Attest writes target certificate then selects/reads it and relies on outer fallback resolution, so a failing completion callback can abandon a disposable certificate. Other metadata APIs preserve exact20-byte fingerprint and signed-int bit-write semantics.
OpenPgpSession.Pin.cs: Both User modes use P2 correctly but extended logical identity selects Reset for KDF and retry fallback. KDF-derived inputs/combined arrays clear in finally; caller inputs stay borrowed. Two-mode Unverify, lazy F9 lookup and fallback C4 are separate exchanges. Change/reset routes differ deliberately; failures become either broad typed VERIFY or ordinary APDU exceptions. Generic Core guards supply no complete credential workflow lease.
OpenPgpSession.Reset.cs: Reset reads retry counts, attempts invalid VERIFY, ignores E6/44 status and reuses the backend for select/version/app-data refresh. It discards reread version, retains original effective policy and inherited auth/readiness, drops KDF without disposal and clears UIF overrides. SCP reset gets no new handshake. PIN-block loop early-stops only on6983 and otherwise assumes its attempted count suffices; preserve incomplete postcondition and ATT exception.
OpenPgpSession.cs: ConstructInitialized binds before SELECT, registers protocol, reads detected version, configures override/detected version with optional SCP, rebinds backend and populates app cache before readiness. Raw GetData exposes response-owned memory; PutData borrows payload with no cache update. Presence derives slot policy with cached/direct/fallback paths. KDF load broadly falls back after ApduException. Derived disposal clears current KDF before sync base drain but after async core teardown.
PinPolicy.cs: Always consumes signature authorization; Once follows card access state rather than managed session lifetime. Current XML names selection/reset/unverify boundaries accurately. Retain the useful clarification and keep executable sample wording tracked separately.
PrivateKeyImport.cs: Import borrows caller SDK keys, selects module-supported representation, pads ordinary components, reverses X25519 scalar and clears only its owned copies. Ed25519 borrows the key seed. NEO path advertises CRT02 while emitting modulus; no Core catalog/provider change resolves that applet wire mismatch. Error catch disposes already collected owned buffers.
PrivateKeyTemplate.cs: Template borrows components through serialization, creates copied TLVs and clears values/inner encodings in finally while disposing all returned components. Result is a separate caller-owned encoding cleared by PutKey. Public headers/CRT need no secret clearing. Partial allocation inside GetComponents can fail before the outer components scope receives owners; avoid a universal allocation-failure cleanup claim.
PublicAPI.Shipped.txt: The shipped snapshot contains only nullable enable and has no assigned semantic unit. Preserve the disposition-only path without inventing a method/type or coverage unit.
PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt: The complete API snapshot was reconciled with current public declarations: SmartCard factory/convenience entry, Core KeyType metadata navigation, KDF/public collection shapes and forty interface methods. Generated record/accessor syntax needs no invented prose. Preserve bytes; signature data proves no compiler or device gate.
Pw.cs: Logical User/Reset/Admin values intentionally overlap VERIFY User-other-mode byte82. Current Reset XML explicitly separates recovery identity from access-mode encoding, preserving the confirmed identity defect rather than normalizing it as intended behavior.
PwStatus.cs: Seven raw bytes map policy/limits/retries, unknown policy falls to Once and raw format bits remain inside integer limits. GetMaxLen/GetAttempts select logical credentials and reject invalid enum values. Literal tests cover ordinary counts/limits, not format-bit parsing or all card profiles.
RsaImportFormat.cs: The four numeric formats distinguish standard/standard+modulus/CRT/CRT+modulus. NEO PrivateKeyImport currently chooses02 with an N component; model values are accurate and the caller mismatch stays applet-owned.
RsaSize.cs: The public enum models2048/3072/4096 only; Core RSA1024 is intentionally absent from OpenPGP metadata. Size availability remains card/slot/firmware-specific.
SecuritySupportTemplate.cs: Counter parsing accepts variable1..4+ widths and defaults missing/empty to zero; normal card counter is three-byte. Current XML correctly records signature-key import/generation and application reset effects, without treating metadata as independent provenance.
SupportedAlgorithm.cs: Each immutable entry owns references to slot/attributes; ordered repeated slots are preserved by the session list. This reports interpreted card information rather than selecting a default or attesting provider/card operation support.
Uif.cs: Policy values, Button encoding and first-byte parse remain straightforward. Current fixed-policy XML distinguishes ordinary key replacement/reset from ATT's irreversible replacement requirement and malformed CRT constraint. The enum creates no actual touch event or callback lifetime.
Yubico.YubiKit.OpenPgp.csproj: Shipping project references Core and opts into shared NativeAOT analyzer/metadata properties; description accurately says raw deciphering/agreement rather than content encryption. Preserve source/newline identity and separate project declaration from compilation/AOT runtime acceptance.
tests/CLAUDE.md: The nested instruction distinguishes unit versus integration projects and directs tests to the repository wrapper. This source-only return invokes no runner; full harness and evidence policy remain later gates.
OpenPgpAdvancedTests.cs: The KDF test derives initial hashes, installs an aliased object, changes equal old/new credentials and checks cached properties plus ordinary verification; no fresh reload/extended transition proof. Generation tests mostly inspect attrs/public-key nonemptiness; Ed25519 checks64-byte output only. Initial hash finally does not clear all KDF/source/result copies and helper leaves state after body.
OpenPgpDecryptTests.cs: RSA imports a host key and compares plaintext; P256 compares returned raw secret to host agreement with the same keys, a meaningful independent operation oracle. RSA's early return covers4.2.0..4.3.5 inclusive before setup despite imported-key mitigation. OpenPgpKeyImportTests.cs: RSA/P256/P384 and Aut imports verify card signatures using host-generated keys. Ed25519/X25519 import tests compare published RFC public points only; X25519 agreement remains untested. Helper parses7F49/86 using Core TLV copies. Host-exported private arrays and signature/result lifetimes retain the old cleanup finding; old RSA early return preserves exact inclusive bound.
OpenPgpMultiCurveTests.cs: P384 and Brainpool generation check attributes, public-key nonemptiness and/or generated status; signature case checks nonempty, never host verification. Retry configuration writes recovery code then5/3/5 and reads those counters; helper restores nothing after body. Core catalog support is not additional real-device evidence.
OpenPgpPinManagementTests.cs: Reset-code/admin recovery block User via attempted wrong PINs, assert User zero then verify replacement PIN. Unverify only probes subsequent signing failure, and an Always policy could already consume authorization; this test neither controls policy nor demonstrates a second signature before Unverify. It is not an isolated causal proof of both modes clearing. Signature policy test reads stored bytes only; unauthorized generation checks exception type rather than exact SW. Preserve meaningful source statements without strengthening their oracles.
OpenPgpSessionTests.cs: All methods and helper calls were read: reset asserts3/0/3 only; generated signatures/public data mostly shape; certificate CRUD compares bytes; attestation checks decoded/nonempty and overwrite under ordinary User mode, not trust/key binding. Four-slot fingerprint/time expectations remain old-family qualifications. Two unequal challenges are no RNG qualification. Two RSA methods early-return through4.3.5; successful body operations leave state to external restoration.
OpenPgpTestStateExtensions.cs: WithConnectionAsync owns the connection; separate using reset session is plain and disposed before body creation. Body receives optional config/SCP and action is awaited before synchronous session disposal. Optional SCP here supplies no test that resets an SCP session; no final reset/readback occurs. Caller owns parameters and all detached action work would escape the represented scope.

Roundtrips share production encoder/decoder; exact independent literals have stronger wire identity scope. The X25519 Aut factory case proves identifier selection, not supported card slot. Repeated parse test mutates original encoding and compares distinct actual fingerprint backing arrays, a meaningful ownership oracle. HistoricalBytes test only checks nonempty; it does not prove all optional field contents or unknown-profile behavior.
OpenPgpAuditReproTests.cs: Slot import test inspects first short-chain CRT after attribute write; short-count S2K compares host SHA256 of explicit input, unsigned count checks encode/decode and one-above case names exact bytes. Libgcrypt-named tests compare retained literals while executing SDK only. Literal provenance remains historical qualification and no test ran in this packet.
BcdHelperTests.cs: Six valid single-byte BCD vectors and multi-byte valid/zero/high-invalid/low-invalid serial cases are explicit. These establish local arithmetic/admission assertions, not full GET VERSION response validation or firmware provenance.
DigestInfoTests.cs: SHA256/384/512 literal headers are compared byte-exact; unsupported algorithm checks dispatch; Build checks total51, prefix and digest endpoint placement rather than full emitted-body equality. Retain that exact oracle scope and host/card padding distinction.
KdfTests.cs: Tests distinguish raw KdfNone, byte-count SHA256 transcripts, length-only SHA512, unequal-salt outputs, null salt fallback, encode/parse fields and exact multiples. Several objects/output hashes remain undisposed/uncleared. Unknown algorithm fixture maps to KdfNone, without actually supplying empty input despite the method name. No transition or live credential identity proof is supplied by model tests.
OpenPgpAidTests.cs: Known AID fields/raw bytes and one low-high-bit invalid-BCD negative serial are asserted. The fixture does not test the high-bit raw value that can produce a positive signed result; current public XML already preserves that condition. Too-short check alone is not the substantive sampling nominee.
OpenPgpCollectionContractTests.cs: Reflection asserts sealed object-derived read-only dictionary contracts, absence of mutable dictionary interfaces/public constructors. It does not assert immutable byte storage, parsed content or device state; ApplicationRelatedData tests carry the distinct array-ownership oracle.
OpenPgpInvalidPinExceptionTests.cs: Fake responses check63Cx,6983,6982/User/Admin/extended Reset count and unavailable count. Extended test intentionally records the defect. CancelOnPwStatusLookupConnection cancels its own CTS and returns Task.FromCanceled regardless of supplied token; the test proves exception propagation rather than admitted native cancellation. Recorder/application-data helpers were read completely; F9 6A82 is broad fallback evidence, not absence.
OpenPgpKeyInfoTests.cs: Independent dotted OID/value-octet literals cover all nine EC representations, lookup None rejection, optional RSA/symmetric metadata and RFC8410 distinction. These exact representation assertions are substantive and stay separate from provider execution, firmware/slot support and X25519 agreement.
OpenPgpPutKeyWireTests.cs: Complete helpers reassemble outgoing APDU chunks, parse4D/7F48/5F48 and compare requested ordinary CRT/component bytes. Exponent rejection precedes wire; nonchangeable attrs branch is explicit. Named non-NIST scalar1 tests compare literal attributes/template and require a host provider with skip on unsupported curves. OpenPgpSessionWireTests.cs: Complete synthetic responses, queue/command/prompt helpers and all bodies were read. UIF/cache/request-failure/pre-admission cancel/status paths are explicit. Signature helpers retain actual arrays for successful transfer and failure erasure; Decrypt resolution only checks exception/outcome. Cached-KDF disposal checks an aliased salt after async disposal, while throwing-KDF test checks sync detach. No held whole-workflow, native release, SCP reset, F9 replacement-disposal or certificate-resolution-failure oracle exists.
PrivateKeyTemplateTests.cs: The custom descriptor helper independently parses one/two-byte BER lengths; tests inspect tags, concatenated components, optional public field count and header/value widths using deliberately tiny noncryptographic key data. They establish serialization layout, not provider-valid keys, all byte equality or card import. Sensitive fixture encodings/dictionary copies are not comprehensively cleared.
PwStatusTests.cs: Seven-byte literals assert policy/three limits/retries and logical lookup selection; raw format bits, unknown policies and extended-mode identity are outside these tests. The default fixture explicitly uses Always, distinct from historical reset hardware Once; no universal device default is inferred.
Yubico.YubiKit.OpenPgp.UnitTests.csproj: Unit project uses xunitv3 MTP executable with explicit library and private Tests.Shared reference; no traditional TestSDK runner is declared. Keep test framework distinctions and no-runtime source outcome explicit.
